questions.stem: What is the monomer used to make poly(chloroethene), commonly known as PVC?
questions.explanation: PVC (poly(chloroethene)) is made from the monomer chloroethene (CH2=CHCl), also known as vinyl chloride. The C=C double bond opens up during addition polymerisation, and the chlorine atoms appear on alternate carbon atoms in the polymer chain.

questions.stem: How do you identify the monomer from a given addition polymer structure?

options.text: Remove the brackets and add water molecules
Find the repeating unit in brackets and change the C-C single bond back to a C=C double bond
Break all the bonds and count the atoms
Add -OH groups to each end of the repeating unit

questions.explanation: To identify the monomer from an addition polymer, find the repeating unit shown in brackets. Then change the C-C single bond in the backbone back to a C=C double bond and add hydrogen atoms as needed. This reverses the process of addition polymerisation.
